title: The characteristic pressure outlet's reflection of a plane pulse: the one-pole (Selle) response in time
source: L. Selle, F. Nicoud, T. Poinsot, 'Actual impedance of nonreflecting boundary conditions: implications for computation of resonators', AIAA J. 42(5):958–964, 2004 (the relaxed outlet's R(ω) = −1/(1 − 2iω/K), so |R| = K/√(K² + 4ω²): a one-pole low-pass of rate K/2 applied to a fully reflected wave); T. J. Poinsot, S. K. Lele, 'Boundary conditions for direct simulations of compressible viscous flows', J. Comput. Phys. 101:104–129, 1992 (the boundary treatment); D. H. Rudy, J. C. Strikwerda, 'A nonreflecting outflow boundary condition for subsonic Navier–Stokes calculations', J. Comput. Phys. 36:55–70, 1980 (σ ≈ 0.25)

quantities.quantity: σ 1.0: the largest departure of the characteristic outlet's reflection from the one-pole response (rate K/2) to the uniform outlet's, over the incident peak, up to step 7268
quantities.reason: the one-pole response leaves out the outlet closure's own direct reflection, measured at 2.28·10⁻³ of the incident peak and the same at σ 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 (so not from the relaxation); the tolerance is 1.75 times that, so a doubling of it fails

quantities.quantity: σ 1.0: the decay rate fitted to the reflection's tail, over K/2
quantities.reason: the record holds 0.54 e-folds of the tail (to step 7268, before the inlet's reflection returns), and the closure's direct reflection sits on it; measured +0.05 %; the tolerance is ten times that

quantities.quantity: σ 0.25 (the default): the largest departure of the characteristic outlet's reflection from the one-pole response (rate K/2) to the uniform outlet's, over the incident peak, up to step 7268
quantities.reason: the one-pole response leaves out the outlet closure's own direct reflection, measured at 2.28·10⁻³ of the incident peak and the same at σ 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 (so not from the relaxation); the tolerance is 1.75 times that, so a doubling of it fails

quantities.quantity: σ 0.25: the decay rate fitted to the reflection's tail, over K/2
quantities.reason: the record holds only 0.13 e-folds of the tail (time constant 2/K = 28,000 steps), so the fit is looser than at σ 1.0; measured +0.54 %; the tolerance is about four times that

quantities.quantity: the control: the uniform outlet's reflected over incident peak (a pressure-release end, |R| = 1)
quantities.reason: the pulse also spreads by viscosity (τ 0.51) between its two passes of the probe, and the closure's direct reflection is part of it; measured 0.9928

quantities.quantity: σ 0.25: windowed spectral ratio at ω 0.01 rad/step, includes the truncated relaxation tail (reflected over incident pulse, rectangular windows of ±346 steps); not the outlet's |R| at ω 0.01
quantities.reason: the reference is the same window applied to the one-pole response to the uniform outlet's reflection (this runner's number, not |R|); the measurement adds the closure's direct reflection, which the one-pole response leaves out: measured less reference is −0.0025, +0.0041 and +0.0019 at ω 0.01, 0.02 and 0.04, and the tolerance 0.005 covers the largest. The fixture freezes this runner's value
